synoptic.summary: The high is moving east and pressure is falling fast ahead of a trough from the Pacific Northwest. Friday brings increasing flow from 160°–200° (20–34 kt from 3,400 to 9,200 ft above landing) and isolated afternoon showers. A cold front comes down the Wasatch Front early Saturday (04:00–07:00) with moderate rain, and the flow turns to 300°–345° behind it. The flow behind the front is fairly weak (up to ~19 kt) and fades by midday. Showers end Saturday evening, and a ridge builds back in for Sunday with very light winds aloft (2–8 kt below 5,500 ft above landing) and a shallow morning inversion. More storms are due Tuesday/Wednesday and late next week.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: The trough will bring a cold front into the Wasatch Front that stretches down the I-15 corridor between 4-7am. This will bring a line of moderate rain with isolated pockets of heavier precipitation.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure was 1016.4 mb at 17:54 Thursday, down 8.6 mb in 23 hours (1025.0 mb). The high has gone and a front is approaching: Friday gets worse through the day, Saturday is the frontal day, and pressure should rise again with the ridge on Sunday.

observations.summary: Thursday-evening observations (17:35–18:15 local). They are current but say little about Friday morning. Spanish Fork and Alpine report flow from 340°–015° at 7–12 kt (evening flow from the north). Lehi already reports drainage-type flow from 130°–140° at 6–8 kt. The Salt Lake airport and South Valley Regional are calm, and Provo reports 310°/4 kt. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no data.

d2-am.explanation: The southerly gradient is building ahead of Saturday's front. Before 10:00 the launch wind is forecast from 140°–150° with 15–18 kt from 152°–159° just above, which is the rotor setup for this site. By the time it turns to 160°, the 20–28 kt flow above is mixing down, and the airport forecast gusts to 23 kt from 11:00. Only a steady 160°+ sock under light wind early would change this, and nothing in the data points to it.
